title: Vows belong to the Lord alone, not to Saints as gods by participation or as obtainers of goods
source_text: XXVIII. Idem sentiunt de votis, quae Scriptura Domino soli concipi & exsolvi jubet, nec putant minus a vera pietate abhorrere, ut quis voveat Sanctis, quatenus sunt Dii quidam per participationem, vel impetratores bonorum quibus egemus, quam ut quis sub eodem titulo iis offerat sacrificia & victimas.
pass_a_gloss: They think the same of vows, which Scripture commands to be conceived and paid to the Lord alone, nor do they think it less abhorrent to true piety that someone should vow to the Saints, insofar as they are certain gods by participation, or obtainers of the goods we need, than that someone under the same title should offer them sacrifices and victims.
pass_b_english: Vows, Scripture says, are to be made and paid to the Lord alone.
To vow to Saints as gods by participation, or as those who obtain what we need, is as contrary to true piety as offering them sacrifices under the same title.

choices.why: Even the softer Roman title, impetrator, does not make a vow lawful.
rejected: mere witnesses of a vow to God
